summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR 1,197 crore (+15.2% YoY), but margins compressed on material cost and a pricing lag from the Middle East conflict.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue reached INR 1,197 crore, the highest single quarter, up 15.2% YoY, with PBT of INR 196.6 crore (+16.4%) and PAT of INR 146.3 crore (+15.5%). FY26 revenue was INR 4,302 crore (+9.2%), PBT INR 693 crore (+13.9%) and PAT INR 517 crore (+12.2%). Management attributed the Q4 margin fall (about 230 bps QoQ) to material cost increases from supply constraints and the Middle East conflict, plus a January salary increase, with customer price recovery still under negotiation. The board approved a 5:1 bonus issue and a final dividend of INR 4 per share post bonus.

segments.name: OE (original equipment)
segments.commentary: Q4 OE sales grew about 25% YoY; FY26 OE sales grew 17.5-17.6% to INR 1,978 crore, outperforming an industry where >6t vehicle production rose 16.6% to 463,000 units. Q4 >6t production hit a record 151,000 units (+26.9%).

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Q4 aftermarket grew about 21% YoY to INR 151 crore; FY26 revenue INR 583-584 crore (+15.5-15.6%). Network expanded by 51 distributor branches and 14 service centres.

segments.name: Exports (goods)
segments.commentary: Q4 exports fell about 6% YoY per the call, with Europe up about 6% and the Americas down about 22%; FY26 exports INR 1,025 crore (-11.1%). Management guided to moderate improvement, with early US recovery signs in Q4.

segments.name: Export services (engineering)
segments.commentary: Export of services grew 22.5% YoY in Q4 and 15.4% for FY26, driven by engineering work for global centres; service income for FY26 was INR 509 crore (+10%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating margin expected to be broadly flat, with at most single-digit growth; management was cautious given the Middle East conflict and government calls for expense control.
FY27 capex guided at INR 180-190 crore, covering new product capex plus replacements and upgrades.
April and May 2026 volumes were described as better than prior years, with Q1 expected to be a good quarter.
Final dividend of INR 4 per share post bonus; bonus issue 5:1 with record date 24 June 2026 and deemed allotment 25 June 2026, subject to approvals; AGM and dividend record date 10 July 2026.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at INR 180-190 crore, split between new products and replacement/upgrade spend.

Oragadam multidivisional plant: new lines for crankshaft machining, ASP cartridges and vacuum pump commissioned; management said Mahindra World City utilisation is near peak and further expansion will be at Oragadam.
Jamshedpur rainwater harvesting pond of 1,200 kL to meet about 40% of plant water needs; Ambattur organic waste converter commissioned.
Assembly capabilities strengthened at Jamshedpur and Lucknow; OMA maturity assessment completed with a good score across Ambattur, Mahindra World City, Lucknow and Jamshedpur.
demand_pricing: Q4 margin fell about 230 bps QoQ on higher material costs (aluminium up from about INR 233/kg to INR 274/kg, roughly 18% of material cost) and a January salary increase; price recovery talks with customers are ongoing and lag costs.
ESC is voluntarily fitted in POL/tanker trucks today; regulation kicks in from October 2027 for vehicles above 6t, and management expects value per vehicle to rise as ESC penetration increases.
ADAS: management has won full-suite business from 2 OEMs; discussions are ongoing with most other OEMs, with several competitors also engaged.
Management said OEMs are increasingly splitting ESC and AEBS/ADAS across partners, while AEBS/ADAS (5 mandated features) is typically sourced from a single partner.
Q3 to Q4 value per vehicle drop was attributed to one-off retrospective selling price variances recognised in Q3; excluding them, value per vehicle was roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall about 230 bps QoQ, and what is the FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher material costs from supply constraints and the Middle East conflict, plus a January salary increase, with no one-offs. FY27 margin is expected to be broadly flat with single-digit growth, with caution on the macro outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA growth lag revenue growth in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost increases from the war and commodity prices came ahead of customer price recoveries, creating a timing lag that management expects to correct over time.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q4 segment growth rates and blended export decline?
qa_highlights.answer: OE grew about 25%, aftermarket about 21%, exports fell about 6%, and export services rose 22.5%. Europe grew about 6%, the Americas fell about 22%, and the blended export decline was about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of diesel price hikes on demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher diesel prices would hit freight rates and truck utilisation, which could slow vehicle purchases with a lag. Replacement demand for inefficient old trucks could offset this.

qa_highlights.question: How does ADAS and AEBS sourcing work with ESC?
qa_highlights.answer: ESC and ADAS can be sourced from separate suppliers, but AEBS and ADAS are typically awarded to one partner able to demonstrate all 5 mandated features.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for US exports and the FY30 India localisation target?
qa_highlights.answer: The US export gap versus two years ago is still about 20%, though US vehicle production has risen for four months. Management said new RFQs are coming in and the group's India growth commitment stands.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and commodity cost inflation (aluminium) squeezing margins until customer price recoveries are agreed.
Diesel price hike may reduce freight rates and truck utilisation, delaying vehicle purchases.
US export volumes still about 20% below two years ago; Americas down about 22% in Q4.
Timing of ESC and ADAS mandate from October 2027 and the pace of further OEM ADAS awards.
Q3 one-off selling price variances distorted value per vehicle; watch the Q1 FY27 reading.
Supplier constraints and gas shortages seen earlier in FY26 could recur.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and long-term regulatory drivers, but cautious on FY27 margins and the macro outlook, citing the Middle East conflict and commodity costs. Management was vaguer on the US export recovery and India sourcing timelines.
